summary: Overview of Saudi Arabia's geography: a Southwest Asian country occupying 80% of the Arabian Peninsula with coastlines on the Persian Gulf and Red Sea. Many of its borders with neighbors are undefined, so its exact area is uncertain, with estimates between about 2.15 and 2.24 million sq km. Very little land is arable, and population is concentrated in coastal areas and interior oases.
one_line: Saudi Arabia occupies most of the Arabian Peninsula, has strategic Gulf and Red Sea coasts, undefined borders, uncertain area, and little arable land.
key_facts: The Kingdom of Saudi Arabia is situated in Southwest Asia and is the largest country of Arabia.
Saudi Arabia borders the Persian Gulf and the Red Sea and lies north of Yemen.
Its coastlines on the Persian Gulf and Red Sea give it great leverage on shipping, especially crude oil, through the Persian Gulf and Suez Canal.
The kingdom occupies 80% of the Arabian Peninsula.
Most of Saudi Arabia's boundaries with the UAE, Oman, and the Republic of Yemen are undefined, so the country's exact size is unknown.
The Republic of Yemen was formerly two countries: the Yemen Arab Republic (North Yemen) and the People's Democratic Republic of Yemen (South Yemen).
The Saudi government estimates the country's area at 2,217,949 square kilometres.
Other reputable estimates of Saudi Arabia's area range between 2,149,690 and 2,240,000 sq. kilometres.
Less than 1% of Saudi Arabia's total area is suitable for cultivation.
In the early 1990s, Saudi population distribution varied greatly among eastern and western coastal towns, densely populated interior oases, and vast, almost empty deserts.
